text:
Jessica: CI microbench failed on PR 10678 — batcher_latency_median +12% vs golden. Not just noise, visible across 3 runs.
Kevin: ugh. Which microbench? the continuous-batcher one?
Jessica: yes, `bench/batcher/warmup_plateau` (seq=128 path). Error visible in the CI diff artifacts: `threshold_diff: +12.4% median latency`.
Maria: leaving a quick note: PR touches kernel_selector heuristics (autoselect cost model) and the prefetch/batch-timer twist. Could be interaction.
Jessica: I pulled the CI artifacts: KV hit rate drops ~2.7% at steady-state, batch wait time distribution shifted right. Suspect batching timer or kernel path causing slower per-token.
ci-bot: @channel CI perf run #pr-10678: microbench-batcher/warmup_plateau failed threshold (median +12.4%). Full artifacts: https://ci.redwood.example/artifacts/pr-10678/bench-2951234567
Kevin: can someone repro locally? I can run bench harness on an r5g with same docker image.
Sam: I'll try repro with commit range local bisect. Quick test: `./bench/run.py --bench batcher/warmup_plateau --runs 5 --seq 128 --model small`
Jessica: FYI I ran that locally on a dev GPU: reproducible. Attaching a short perf trace snippet — main hotspot moves from `kv_cache_lookup` to `kernel_dispatcher::select_kernel`.
Maria: interesting. that points to kernel selection path being heavier for short sequences because of extra heuristics introduced. The PR added a fallthrough cost-estimation pass.
Kevin: if kernel_select is expensive per-inference, batching can amplify cost (selector runs per batch or per request?). Where is it invoked?
Jessica: selector called at batch creation time for each pipeline path. With the new path we added a safety re-eval that walks through candidate kernels and runs a micro-cost estimate (cheap math ops but still ~200us each). With high batch churn that accumulates.
Sam: can we memoize by (model, seq_len, quant, device) key for the CI runs? Quick patch: cache selector result for 30s.
Maria: tried a quick cache in local branch -> bench median delta drops to +1.3% (within noise). So cache fixes it. But that hides the underlying extra cost — still a regression in selector complexity.
Jessica: For CI bisect I reverted the selector commit locally and bench returns to golden. Bisect points to commit `8f3b2a7` (the heuristics pass).
Kevin: plan: 1) revert heuristics in PR to unblock rollout; 2) file follow-up to rework selector with lightweight estimates and a small LRU cache keyed by (model_hash, seq_bucket). 3) add perf unit that asserts selector per-request cost < X micros.
ci-bot: @Jessica opened issue PERF-2314: "kernel selector per-request cost regression after heuristics" (https://jira.redwood.example/browse/PERF-2314)
Maria: also add telemetry: histogram for selector_latency in runtime traces so we can detect regression in CI next time.
Sam: I'm going to push a small revert commit to pr-10678 branch and rerun CI. Will post results.
Kevin: if revert lands, add a temporary skip marker on the new unit test until we ship the optimized selector.
Jessica: Revert pushed -> CI rerun queued. If green, we can merge and then follow up with PERF-2314.
ci-bot: CI run for pr-10678 (revert) started: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/2951234599
Sam: CI passed the microbench (median diff +0.4%). Rolling back the heuristics unblocks release.
Maria: Logged notes for the follow-up: profiling flamegraph link + sample command:
```
# reproduce locally
./bench/run.py --bench batcher/warmup_plateau --runs 10 --seq 128 --model small --profile /tmp/fg.svg
# run selector microbench
./tools/selector_bench --model small --seq 128 --iters 10000
```
Jessica: Thanks all. We'll keep the perf test added in the PR but mark it as flaky until selector optimization is implemented. Adding owners: @Maria + @Kevin. :thumbsup:
Sam: TL;DR: kernel-selector heuristics increased per-request cost; caching/revert restores perf; follow-up to rework heuristics and add selector latency monitoring.
